Odin × Godot

The ScriptLanguageExtension surface (Godot 4.6.2) — implementation reference

12 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
1. GDExtensionScriptInstanceInfo3 — per-node dispatch (the hot path)2. ScriptExtension — one per .odin file (OdinScript, 37 virtuals)3. ScriptLanguageExtension — the singleton (OdinLanguage, 60 virtuals)Dispatch and registration requirementsEditor developer-experience features (implemented)

This implementation record describes the engine version named above and the validation/completion work measured during that implementation. Its counts, timings, and phase references retain that scope. For current script authoring and editor setup, use the authoring guide and Workflow.

The implementation plan covered three engine interfaces, extracted from the pinned engine's extension_api.json and gdextension_interface.h:

  • ScriptLanguageExtension — 60 virtual methods (the language singleton, OdinLanguage)
  • ScriptExtension — 37 virtual methods (one per .odin resource, OdinScript)
  • GDExtensionScriptInstanceInfo3 — 26 function pointers (per-node instance dispatch)

The plan assigned each of the 123 entry points a tier: MUST (core behavior), SHOULD (editor/tooling polish), or STUB (return a safe default — empty list / false / nil). Phase numbers refer to PLAN.md. Cross-referenced against the miniml_godot reference, which shipped with a working subset.

examples/hello/ verified the registration mechanism. OdinLanguage and OdinScript register as GDExtension classes derived from ScriptLanguageExtension / ScriptExtension. get_virtual_func maps each virtual name to a function pointer, as in the hello _process example. The per-instance vtable is passed to script_instance_create3.

1. GDExtensionScriptInstanceInfo3 — per-node dispatch (the hot path)#

Engine lifecycle, method, and signal calls enter Odin through this interface. call_func dispatches method calls.

fn ptr tier phase notes
call_func MUST 2 dispatch a method name → registered Odin proc; convert Variant args to typed params. _process/_physics_process/signal handlers/custom methods all arrive here.
notification_func MUST 2 NOTIFICATION_READY(13)/ENTER_TREE/EXIT_TREE/etc. → lifecycle procs. _ready arrives as a notification, not a call (miniml: it's deferred a frame).
get_owner_func MUST 2 return the node Object* (stored at instance create).
get_script_func MUST 1 return the OdinScript Object*.
get_language_func MUST 1 return the OdinLanguage singleton.
free_func MUST 2 free the Odin instance struct + env.
has_method_func MUST 2 does the registered class have this method?
set_func / get_func MUST 3 @export property write/read (field at offset in the Odin struct).
get_property_list_func / free_property_list_func MUST 3 report @export vars to Inspector/serializer.
get_property_type_func SHOULD 3 Variant type of a property.
get_method_list_func / free_method_list_func SHOULD 3 enumerate methods (editor/introspection).
get_method_argument_count_func SHOULD 3 arg count for a method.
property_can_revert_func / property_get_revert_func STUB 3 default value revert (return false).
validate_property_func STUB 3 Inspector tweaks (no-op).
to_string_func STUB 6 "<OdinScript:Class>".
refcount_incremented_func / refcount_decremented_func STUB — for RefCounted-based scripts; default.
is_placeholder_func STUB — false (we instantiate real).
set_fallback_func / get_fallback_func STUB — dynamic prop fallback (nil).
get_class_category_func STUB — Inspector grouping (nil).
get_property_state_func SHOULD 3 serialize live property values (for reload/save).

2. ScriptExtension — one per .odin file (OdinScript, 37 virtuals)#

method tier phase notes
_get_language MUST 1 the OdinLanguage singleton.
_can_instantiate MUST 1 true at runtime (false for tool-only in editor unless @tool).
_instance_create MUST 2 build a script instance (ScriptInstanceInfo3 + Odin struct) for an owner node.
_get_instance_base_type MUST 2 the extends base class name (e.g. CharacterBody2D).
_has_source_code / _get_source_code / _set_source_code MUST 1 the .odin text.
_reload MUST 4 recompile + re-bind live instances (hot reload).
_has_method MUST 2 registered class has method?
_is_tool MUST 1 @tool scripts run in editor.
_is_valid MUST 1 compiled/registered OK?
_get_script_property_list MUST 3 @export vars.
_get_script_signal_list / _has_script_signal MUST 3 declared signals.
_get_script_method_list / _get_method_info / _get_script_method_argument_count SHOULD 3 method introspection.
_has_property_default_value / _get_property_default_value SHOULD 3 @export defaults.
_get_base_script / _inherits_script SHOULD 3 script inheritance chain (likely nil — Odin extends engine classes, not other scripts, at least initially).
_get_global_name SHOULD 3 class_name-equivalent for cross-script typing/autoload.
_has_static_method SHOULD 3 static methods.
_get_rpc_config SHOULD 5 multiplayer RPC annotations.
_placeholder_instance_create / _placeholder_erased / _is_placeholder_fallback_enabled / _instance_has STUB — editor placeholder instances; default.
_editor_can_reload_from_file SHOULD 4 true (enables editor reload).
_is_abstract STUB — false.
_get_member_line SHOULD 6 editor go-to-symbol (via odin source map).
_get_constants / _get_members STUB — empty.
_update_exports SHOULD 3 refresh Inspector after edit.
_get_doc_class_name / _get_documentation / _get_class_icon_path STUB 6 docs.

3. ScriptLanguageExtension — the singleton (OdinLanguage, 60 virtuals)#

Identity & registration — MUST (Phase 1)#

_get_name("Odin"), _get_type("OdinScript"), _get_extension("odin"), _get_recognized_extensions(["odin"]), _get_reserved_words(Odin keywords), _get_comment_delimiters(["//","/* */"]), _get_string_delimiters(["" ""," "]), _create_script(→ OdinScript), _init, _finish, _make_template, _supports_builtin_mode(false), _can_inherit_from_file(false at first), _is_using_templates, _get_built_in_templates.

Threading — MUST-stub (Phase 2)#

_thread_enter / _thread_exit — set up/tear down the Odin context per engine thread (or assert main-thread-only, like miniml). The resource loader runs off the main thread.

Reload — Phase 4#

_reload_all_scripts, _reload_scripts, _reload_tool_script — drive the recompile+swap.

Editor tooling — SHOULD (Phase 6)#

_validate (run odin check, map diagnostics to line/col), _validate_path, _lookup_code, _complete_code, _auto_indent_code, _find_function, _make_function, _can_make_function, _open_in_external_editor, _overrides_external_editor, _preferred_file_name_casing, _is_control_flow_keyword, _get_doc_comment_delimiters, _supports_documentation, _has_named_classes, _frame (miniml used this to register a syntax highlighter on the editor main thread — deferred because UI isn't ready at init).

_lookup_code (editor "Lookup Symbol") is a stub, but its Dictionary still requires both result and type. ScriptLanguageExtension::lookup_code executes ERR_FAIL_COND_V(!ret.has("type")) even on a failed lookup, so returning only {result} would log Condition "!ret.has("type")" is true. lv_dict_result_failed returns {result: FAILED, type: LOOKUP_RESULT_SCRIPT_LOCATION(0)}.

Global classes / cross-script typing — SHOULD (Phase 3)#

_handles_global_class_type, _get_global_class_name — enables class_name-style autoloads and typed cross-script references (miniml did this via a modules project setting).

STUB (safe defaults — empty/false/nil) unless we add a debugger later#

_get_public_functions, _get_public_constants, _get_public_annotations, _add_global_constant, _add_named_global_constant, _remove_named_global_constant, all 12 _debug_* (stack/locals/expression eval — note: expression eval is impossible in AOT Odin, so the debugger is structural only), all 5 _profiling_*.

Dispatch and registration requirements#

  1. _ready is a notification, not a method call — handle NOTIFICATION_READY in notification_func; _process/_physics_process come through call_func after set_process(true) (set when the registered class defines them).
  2. @export get/set work on struct field offsets captured at registration — this is why the registry stores field layout, and why the generator's new property rendering (in flight) matters for reading/writing engine-side base-class properties.
  3. The whole language is one GDExtension class pair (OdinLanguage/OdinScript) plus a per-instance vtable — not one classdb class per script. The examples/hello/ classdb path proves the primitives; the script path composes them differently.
  4. Most of the 123 entry points are STUBs. Real work concentrates in ~15 MUST methods: instance call/notification/set/get/property_list, script instance_create/ source/reload/base_type, language identity + create_script.

Editor developer-experience features (implemented)#

The recorded editor features use the language singleton and run only natively (core/validate.odin, core/highlighter.odin, core/diag/); the web build gets no-op stubs (core/devtools_web.odin).

_validate — compiler diagnostics#

OdinLanguage._validate(script, path, ...) returns { "valid": bool, "errors": [ { "line", "column", "message" } ] } driving the editor's inline error squiggles + the Errors panel.

  • Whole-package check. A single .odin file is not a compile unit, so validation checks its package: globalize path, take its directory, and run odin check <pkgdir> -collection:godot=<root> -no-entry-point -custom-attribute:gd_method, parsing ‹file›(‹line›:‹col›) Error: ‹msg› / Syntax Error: lines and keeping those whose basename matches the validated file. valid = (errors == 0).
  • Unsaved buffer overlay. script (arg 0) is the possibly-unsaved editor text. We copy the package dir to a temp overlay, overwrite the one edited file with script, then check — so errors update as you type, not only on save. The overlay's *.gen.odin siblings are the last-built ones (stale until the next scriptgen run); existing-code type errors still surface correctly.
  • Collection root config. The <root> for -collection:godot is resolved as: project setting odin_godot/root -> env ODIN_GODOT_ROOT -> the repo default. A consuming project must point one of these at wherever odin_godot lives.
  • Tool-failure fallback. Any failure (can't globalize/copy, odin missing, etc.) returns { valid:true, errors:[] }.
  • Background validation and cache. _validate runs on the editor's main thread after debounced edits. A synchronous odin check rechecked the whole godot binding and blocked the UI for seconds, up to 10-20s cold on a large collection. The implementation moved that work to a background thread:
    • The coordinator in core/diag/async.odin (validate_async) caches completed diagnostics by a content hash of script+path, guarded by sync.Mutex.
    • An exact cache hit returns immediately. A miss schedules run_check_overlay and returns the last completed result. The editor's next debounce retrieves updated diagnostics.
    • At most one worker runs, with one latest pending job. New edits replace that pending job. The worker uses a private heap+temp-arena context and stores Diagnostic{line,col,message} data without accessing Godot/gdext objects. The main thread resolves the odin binary and builds the Godot Dictionary. Recorded first-call latency was ~0.03 ms, compared with a ~34 ms warm (≈0.5 s cold) check; the main thread did not wait for the check.
    • The experiment also evaluated diagnostics through persistent ols. Its src/server/check.odin, configured by odin_command / enable_checker_only_saved, invoked the same odin check on the on-disk package. It was not incremental and showed no validation speed gain in this setup: the warm check was ~34 ms. publishDiagnostics also did not reliably arrive on open/change. Validation therefore retained the async worker, while persistent ols handled autocomplete to avoid indexing the godot collection on every completion request.
  • Reachability / test. The virtual is engine-dispatched and cannot be called from GDScript, so the overlay/check/parse pipeline and async coordinator live in core/diag/ and are checked by tests/validate/: clean fixture -> 0 errors; broken live buffer -> 1 error at the exact line/column; the async path is non-blocking (first-call latency « check duration), eventually correct (broken still flags after the worker finishes), and coalescing (rapid edits keep one worker + one pending). core/validate.odin builds the main-thread Godot response.

_complete_code — autocomplete through a persistent ols session#

OdinLanguage._complete_code(code, path, owner) returns { "result": int(Error), "force": bool, "call_hint": String, "options": Array } (the engine asserts result is present). As the user types, the editor calls it with the full buffer + a U+FFFF caret marker; we drive the ols Odin language server over an unsaved-buffer overlay of the script's package and map its LSP CompletionItems to Godot options (typing gd.node2d_set_p offers node2d_set_position, etc.).

  • Required option fields. Godot's ScriptLanguageExtension::complete_code (core/object/script_language_extension.h, ~L407-420) does ERR_CONTINUE(!op.has("<key>")) on each of kind (int), display (String), insert_text (String), font_color (Color), icon (Ref<Texture2D>, nil ok), default_value (Variant, nil ok), location (int) before reading it — a missing key drops the option and writes an editor error (Condition "!op.has("font_color")" is true ... at: complete_code (...:413)). The canonical key set is declared in core/complete/option_shape.odin (Completion_Option_Field); core/complete.odin builds each option by iterating it (so keys can't drift) and tests/complete asserts it covers the full required set. font_color/icon are placeholders here — the editor recomputes the shown color/icon in CodeTextEditor::_complete_request; only the keys' presence and types matter.

  • Persistent process. The fresh-spawn path (run_completion in core/complete/complete.odin) starts ols, indexes the godot collection (~1059 files), answers one request, and exits. Recorded latency was ~0.5-1.25 s per request. The persistent path (core/complete/session.odin, session_complete) retains one subprocess over bidirectional stdio pipes using core:os. It performs initialize and the ols.json write once, then sends didOpen/didChange and textDocument/completion against the retained index. tests/lsp measured COLD first completion ~0.67 s and WARM completions ~17-19 ms, a ~35-40x speedup for that tested path.

  • Threading. A dedicated reader thread owns ols stdout, parses every Content-Length frame, and hands the awaited response (correlated by request id) to the caller via a cond var; notifications (logMessage, publishDiagnostics) are ignored. Mutexes guard the single in-flight request, stdin writes, the shared session/doc state, and start/teardown. The reader runs on a private heap+temp-arena context and does not touch Godot/gdext. session_complete blocks the calling thread for the request round-trip (warm: tens of ms). The retained index avoids process startup and re-indexing on each completion.

  • Failure and timeout handling. If ols can't start, dies, or a request times out, session_complete returns ok=false and the glue (core/complete.odin) falls back to fresh-spawn run_completion, so a failed persistent session can still attempt completion. A killed ols is detected (reader EOF) and the session restarts on the next call; a short retry backoff prevents repeated rapid process launches; a bogus ols binary fails in ~8 ms. The warn-once-if-ols-missing behavior and the odin_godot/ols_bin -> OLS -> PATH resolution are unchanged. _finish (lv_finish_session) kills the subprocess + reader + temp workspace on editor teardown.

  • Reachability / test. The virtual is engine-dispatched, and tests/lsp/ checks the persistent session for COLD vs WARM latency (asserts warm « cold and warm-avg < 300 ms), node2d_set_position present (generated godot procedures), crash recovery after killing the live ols, clean shutdown, and the bogus-ols fast-fail fallback. tests/complete/ checks the fresh-spawn fallback (run_completion).

Odin syntax highlighter#

OdinSyntaxHighlighter (extends EditorSyntaxHighlighter) token-colors .odin in the Script panel: _get_name->"Odin", _get_supported_languages->["Odin"] (matched against the language name), _create-> a fresh clone, and _get_line_syntax_highlighting(line) -> { start_col(int): { "color": Color } }. The byte-based, rune-column-accurate tokenizer covers keywords (control-flow distinct), // and single-line /* */ comments, string/char /raw-string literals, numbers, PascalCase types, and proc-call identifiers.

  • Deferred registration. Registered on the first editor _frame (guarded by a one-time flag + editor-hint check + a ~30s attempt cap), accessing only ScriptEditor (register_syntax_highlighter) and avoiding EditorHelp, whose doc-gen paths crash on extension classes. The class itself is registered lazily there too, so an exported game (no editor) never registers an editor-only class.
  • Limitations. Block comments are highlighted per-line (an unterminated /* colors to end-of-line); a /* ... */ opened on a previous line is not tracked across lines. Colors use fixed dark-theme constants; reading them from EditorSettings remained a possible refinement. Checking the colors requires a display. tests/editor_smoke verifies registration in a headless editor without crashing; it does not check the rendered colors.
